description: Field names that MUST NOT appear on the current Contrix v1 wire in the contexts listed below. Each entry pins the context (top-level envelope, specific payload class, etc.) because a name may be legal elsewhere. cotest scanner walks Event Envelope / payload bytes and flags any occurrence outside the entry's allowed_contexts.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: Reducer / parser MUST fail with schema_violation when the field appears in the listed context.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Readers MAY tolerate the field during a bounded migration window but writers MUST NOT emit it.
rejection_levels.compat_only: Allowed only on explicit interop / compatibility surfaces.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from machine surfaces; survives in CHANGELOG / migration notes.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: Reference in CHANGELOG or migration documentation.
allowed_context_definitions.legacy_migration: Reference in time-bounded migration code that rewrites stored legacy bytes.
allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: Reference in an explicit interop binding (e.g., MIMI interop) where the cross-protocol mapping requires the field.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert rejection.

entries.notes: Legacy Matrix-style 'branch' top-level field on timeline / Flow events is replaced by the v1 'track' concept (a display-only timeline segment identifier). See current-model 'Track 是纯展示 / 时间线分段标识'. The string 'branch' MUST NOT appear as a top-level Event Envelope or payload field name.
Room core model was removed; Realm is the v1 boundary. 'room_kind' MUST NOT appear on the wire outside an explicit MIMI / Matrix interop module.

Flow payload field 'kind' (or any analogous discriminator) MUST NOT carry the literal value 'room'. Use 'realm' / 'flow' / canonical Realm.kind values. Interop translation lives in an opt-in interop module only.

Pre-inversion Flow payload exposed 'discussion_space_ref' pointing at the (then) security-boundary Space. The canonical field is now 'scope_circle_id' pointing at an intra-Realm Circle (see schemas/flow.schema.json, zh/models/circle.md). The legacy 'discussion_space_ref' MUST NOT appear on the current wire.

entries.replacement: parent_space_id / default_realm_id / scope_circle_id / default_scope_circle_id / retention_policy_id / disclosure_policy_id / rate_limit_policy_id / policy_id
entries.notes: Single concrete protocol object identifiers use `_id`; `_ref` is reserved for causal, proof, schema/profile, content-addressed, or polymorphic reference material. The old fields parent_ref, default_realm_ref, scope_ref, default_scope_ref, retention_policy_ref, disclosure_policy_ref, rate_limit_policy_ref, and Policy-object policy_ref MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.

member_delivery_binding references the policy revision Event that authorized a delivery binding, not a Policy object. The field therefore carries explicit event-reference semantics as policy_event_ref.
The child_scope_policy discriminator now names the concrete field it requires: scope_circle_id.

Range-completeness event_range, audit RYW receipt, and POST /events response previously named the per-Realm frontier slot 'space_frontier'. After the Realm/Space inversion the replication and security boundary that this frontier covers is the Realm (not an in-Realm Space container); the canonical field name is now 'realm_frontier' (see schemas/range-completeness-attestation.schema.json, schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json, OpenAPI EventSubmitResponse). 'space_frontier' MUST NOT appear on the current wire as a frontier object property.

Relation MUST carry rank at the top level, not nested under fields. The dual-source (top-level rank vs fields.rank) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level rank only, and readers MUST reject fields.rank with schema_violation. See zh/models/relation.md §2.
Space MUST carry rank at the top level. Mirrors the relation_payload constraint; closes the dual-source ambiguity uniformly. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.2.

Space is a container, not a security boundary. A cx.space.create / cx.space.update payload carrying Realm-level security_class is the pre-inversion Space-as-boundary shape and MUST be rejected; migrate it to Realm payload fields.

entries.replacement: cx.realm.join_rule or cx.realm.policy_components join policy facet
entries.notes: Join policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry join_rule; this closes the active cx.space.* versus removed pre-inversion payload-shape ambiguity.
History visibility is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry history_visibility.
Policy server attachment is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry policy_server.
Delivery binding policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry delivery_binding_policy.

cx.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. The reducer initializes revision_root to the new message_id; only cx.message.revise (and subsequent revise events) may set revision_root, and only to the create's revision_root. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §9.

cx.content.composite Content Block MUST use the field name `parts` (matching schemas/message.schema.json, schemas/event-payload.schema.json, schemas/flow.schema.json, and schemas/morph.schema.json). The temporary `blocks` spelling was rejected because it over-constrained the concept to document layout blocks; the canonical wire name is `parts`, and `blocks` MUST NOT appear in current content_block_composite wire. See zh/models/content-types.md §4.10.

Encrypted Envelope MUST NOT carry `cleartext_commitment`. The bare cleartext hash is dictionary-attackable offline against low-entropy plaintext; v1 E2EE producers MUST NOT emit it and receivers MUST reject any envelope that carries it (top-level `not.required` in schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json). Future profiles needing plaintext commitment MUST define a keyed/salted form (e.g. the sender_commitment HMAC profile in content-moderation.md §3.4.2).

Flow MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). The dual-source (top-level stage vs fields.stage) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level stage only, and readers MUST reject fields.stage with schema_violation. Same constraint as fields.rank in relation_payload / space_payload. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 and zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.

Flow stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level. It MUST NOT be smuggled under fields.* and MUST NOT be supplied by actor on wire (reducer overwrites with the triggering cx.flow.stage.set event's created_at). See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 rule 3.

entries.replacement: Message on the Flow's discussion track that references the cx.flow.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name guard. Flow stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note / explanation field anywhere — neither on the object, nor in the cx.flow.stage.set payload, nor under fields.*. Human-readable rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' the stage event; audit attribution is provided by the event log's own actor_id / created_at. The fields.stage_reason path MUST be rejected to prevent implementations from re-introducing the field through a back door.

entries.replacement: Message on the Flow's discussion track that references the cx.flow.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name sister-guard for fields.stage_reason. Closes 'stage_note' / 'stage_comment' / 'stage_explanation' style re-spellings via fields.*. Same canonical channel: a Message on the discussion track that references the cx.flow.stage.set event.

entries.replacement: stage (top-level Flow field) or state (physical lifecycle)
entries.notes: Reserved-name guard: 'lifecycle' is reserved terminology for the state axis (cx.<kind>.archive / restore / tombstone lifecycle events). It MUST NOT appear on the wire as a fields.* key on Flow. Business-progression goes through the top-level 'stage' field; physical lifecycle through 'state'. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.

Reserved-name guard: 'progress_state' is a sister name for the stage concept and MUST NOT appear under fields.*. Implementations expressing business progression MUST use the canonical top-level 'stage' field.
Morph MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). Mirror of the flow_payload fields.stage constraint.
Morph stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level.

entries.replacement: Message on an associated discussion track that references the cx.morph.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph. Stage transitions carry no reason field; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message that references the cx.morph.stage.set event.

entries.replacement: Message on an associated discussion track that references the cx.morph.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name sister-guard for Morph fields.stage_reason. Same forbidden surface as Flow.
Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph: 'lifecycle' is reserved for the state axis.
Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph.

cx.flow.update payload's patch MUST NOT include path 'stage' or 'stage_changed_at'. Stage transitions are single-source: only cx.flow.stage.set may mutate these fields. The wire-level guard is the same pattern as forbidding cx.message.create from carrying revision_root — a forbidden patch path on an otherwise-shared payload class. cotest scanners MUST flag any patch op whose path matches /^stage(_changed_at)?$/. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 reducer hard constraint 5.

cx.morph.update / cx.morph.schema_migrate payload's patch MUST NOT include path 'stage' or 'stage_changed_at'. Stage transitions are single-source: only cx.morph.stage.set may mutate these fields. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 reducer hard constraint 6 and zh/models/morph.md §2.

Event proofs MUST bind canonical Event bytes with event_digest. Generic non-Event detached proofs now use payload_digest. payload_hash is forbidden in all wire contexts.

Generic detached-JWS proofs over non-Event canonical payloads (Anchor signature, identity-link, did-continuity, erasure receipts, etc.) MUST use payload_digest. This aligns with the v1 hash-vocabulary rule (common-fields.md §2): output bytes use <noun>_digest; algorithm selector uses <noun>_algorithm; tree roots use <noun>_root. _hash is forbidden as a wire field-name suffix.

Push-notification payload MUST NOT carry the pre-inversion 'space_name' field. After the Realm/Space inversion the human-readable label that a push gateway might surface comes from either the Realm (realm_title) or the Flow (flow_title); both remain forbidden in the cx.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 baseline (privacy default) and are only permitted under the explicit cx.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1 opt-in profile. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §3 and fixtures/privacy-security-fixture.json forbidden_fields_absent.

Generic object_patch_payload single-sources the target object via 'target_ref'. The pre-2026-05-24 draft also accepted 'object_ref' and even target-less patches; both shapes are removed. This forbids only the payload property name; event-payload.schema.json $defs.object_ref and selector grammar object_ref remain valid generic reference terms.

Generic object_lifecycle_payload single-sources the target object via 'target_ref'. The pre-2026-05-24 draft also accepted 'object_ref' or even a target-less {target_state} form; both shapes are removed. This forbids only the payload property name; event-payload.schema.json $defs.object_ref and selector grammar object_ref remain valid generic reference terms.
Federation verification payloads use the v1 hash vocabulary: digest fields end in _digest and values use <algo>:<lowercase_hex>.
MemberIdentity display_profile reuses the canonical avatar_blob_ref name for Blob references.
Applet protocol metadata exposes a Blob reference, so the field carries the _blob_ref suffix.
Media visibility is aligned with Realm / Circle scope; Space is not a security boundary.
Blob metadata uses content_digest with an algorithm prefix. Content-addressed blob_ref values may still use cx:blob:sha256:<hex>.
Blob upload request and response byte counts use size_bytes; bare size is not a byte-count field name in v1.
